overview: This one-page Department of State list of papers indexes three July–August 1932 records concerning Japan’s consolidation of civil, military, diplomatic, and economic authority in Manchuria and the Kwantung Leased Territory. The entries report a Japanese plan to make a special envoy extraordinary and plenipotentiary concurrently commander-in-chief and governor-general, with control over the South Manchuria Railway, followed by the installation of General Nobuyoshi Mutō as governor. The underlying documents were cross-filed under the Department’s Manchuria decimal-file classification and are not reproduced here.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning the Governor-General of Kwantung
subfiles.about: An index lists three records concerning the reorganization of Japanese authority in Kwantung and Manchuria and General Mutō’s installation as governor.
subfiles.summary: The sheet indexes a July 27 Chinese Legation note and two telegrams from Nelson T. Johnson in China, dated July 27 and August 9, 1932. The entries describe proposals to combine the offices of plenipotentiary envoy, commander-in-chief, and governor of Kwantung, while placing the South Manchuria Railway under the same authority. The final entry records General Mutō’s installation as governor of the Kwantung Leased Territory. Each item refers researchers to related documents in file 893.01-Manchuria.

interest: The sheet is useful as a compact archival roadmap to documents filed elsewhere under the Manchuria classification. Its entries reveal how the State Department tracked Japan’s concentration of diplomatic, military, colonial-administrative, and railway authority in a single office during the consolidation of Japanese power in Manchuria in 1932. It also supplies precise cross-references that can reconnect this otherwise skeletal file with the substantive Chinese Legation note and Johnson telegrams.
